headline: A paper frames AI time savings as a joint measurement of workflow time and escaped defects
summary: An October 23 arXiv preprint argues that AI productivity comparisons should report end-to-end time alongside defects escaping independent review. It defines model-free time-saved and excess-defect quantities plus a break-even downstream defect cost. It reanalyzes public data from METR’s 246-issue developer study, reporting slowdown estimates of 19% or 24% depending on the estimand (34% without adjustment for a chance imbalance), and bounds the share of tasks helped at 3–82%. In a prespecified experiment on AI agents reviewing AI-written briefs from SEC filings, one Claude reviewer made fewer checks when told the drafter’s error rate was ten times lower than it was; the paper reports 22.5% of briefs then passed with a wrong figure versus none in the comparison arm. These are paper-reported results, not independent findings.
